text: Vietnamese teacher honoured for risking her life to save student

HÀ NỘI - Phenikaa Group and a delegation from the Ministry of Education and Training visited Hoàng Thị Hiền at Cửa Đông General Hospital in Nghệ An Province on Friday, National Teachers' Day, to honour her bravery in saving a student despite suffering serious injuries herself.

Hiền, a teacher at the Tân Lâm satellite campus of Phú Sơn Kindergarten in Nghĩa Hành Commune, Nghệ An Province, was seriously injured in August 2026 after rushing to pull a child away from an oncoming vehicle on a main road.
The child escaped unharmed, but Hiền suffered severe injuries to both legs in the incident, which has drawn widespread public attention as an example of teachers' dedication to their students.

The delegation included Nguyễn Thị Quyên Thanh, deputy minister of education and training; Lê Đình Nghị, director of the ministry's Department of Personnel and Organisation; and Nguyễn Thanh Đề, director of its Department of Preschool Education, alongside representatives of Nghệ An Province's education department and Phenikaa Group.
During the visit, Thanh presented Hiền with a certificate of commendation from the Minister of Education and Training in recognition of her actions.

Phenikaa Group also provided two savings accounts with a combined value of VNĐ1 billion (US$38,000) for Hiền's children, aiming to offer long-term financial support for their upbringing and education.
"Some of the most meaningful lessons are never written in textbooks.
Hiền has given us a powerful lesson in a teacher's dedication and sense of responsibility," said Trần Lan Phương, deputy general director of Phenikaa Group.
The group expressed its appreciation to Hiền and her family and wished her a speedy recovery, adding that her actions could inspire wider society.
Phenikaa Group said the visit highlighted the role of teachers in not only imparting knowledge but also fostering compassion, kindness and social responsibility.
Education is one of the group's four strategic pillars, alongside industrial manufacturing, technology development and healthcare.

The group said it viewed education as a long-term investment in society and was developing an integrated education system spanning primary, secondary and higher education through institutions including Phenikaa School and Phenikaa University.
It added that the visit reflected its commitment to a people-centred business approach and greater corporate social responsibility. - VNS
